punchline: Attia asks you to name the physical tasks you still want at the end, then train backward from them.
thirty_sec: Attia says medicine mostly aims at lifespan, not at the last ten years, which he calls the marginal decade, when people are alive but cannot do what they enjoy. His Centenarian Decathlon starts from ten physical tasks you want late in life, like getting up from the floor with one arm or carrying groceries, and sets today's training backward from them.
